thread_text:
Ravi: Quick write-up from this morning's load experiments. High level: synthetic steady-state looks optimistic for p99 when KV warmup is disabled; enabling KV warmup narrows the gap. Speculative decoding + int8 gives big p50/cost wins but we saw p99 regressions on long-context traces. More notes below.

Jules: paste the exact commands/envs?

Ravi: sure, ran two controlled variants. configs: 
```
# replay harness (golden trace)
./harness --mode=replay --trace=/mnt/replays/web_long.trace.gz \ 
  --kernel=auto --kv-warmup=on --quant=none --speculative=false --batch=dynamic

# synthetic generator (steady shape)
./harness --mode=synth --profile=web_text --length-dist=realistic --requests=1M \ 
  --kernel=best --kv-warmup=off --quant=int8 --speculative=true --batch=dynamic
```
Ravi: hardware: 8xA100(80GB) per pool, same image, runtime v1.12.4. Aggregation window 1m, but p99 computed from 5m slice.

Eva: any plots?

Ravi: report: <https://redwood.internal/reports/192345|bench results>. TL;DR numbers: p50 cost down ~28% with int8+spec, p99 latency up ~12% on replay long-context. Synth p99 underestimated by ~20% vs replay when kv-warmup=off.

perf-bot: CI: load-compare job finished (id: compare-192345). Artifacts: /artifacts/compare-192345/.

Samir: kernel-level detail — which kernels fell back on long sequences?

Ravi: float path used cuBLAS fused GEMMs most of the time. int8 path picked Triton-fused conv kernels for short contexts, but long sequences hit a generic matmul fallback in the runtime (no fused KV-shim), which increased token compute and memory churn.

Jules: so KV eviction + fallback kernel = p99 spike. quantization increases kv footprint -> more evictions?

Ravi: exactly. With int8 the per-kv-item size changed packing/layout, causing cache pages to be denser and GC/eviction to trigger earlier. When warmup is off, first requests populate cache under different kernel codepaths and some kernels don't implement incremental KV warmup efficiently.

infra-ci: can we reproduce smaller? want a quick PR test.

Ravi: yes, we extracted a 5k-request condensed trace at /mnt/replays/sample_5k.trace.gz. run: `./harness --mode=replay --trace=.../sample_5k.trace.gz --kv-warmup=on|off` should show the divergence within ~2 minutes.

Jules: suggested next steps:
- add an apples-style controlled run that toggles only kv-warmup (keep quant+spec fixed)
- add a kernel-fallback counter to the runtime and emit metric `runtime.kernel_fallback.count`
- run cross-hardware (V100/RTX6000) to see if kernel selection is hardware dependent
- add a regression gate flag so we can block int8+spec in canary if p99 delta > 8%

Samir: for the regression gate, do we want gating at p99 absolute ms or %? seems percent ties to customer SLAs.

Ravi: prefer percent for now, but capture both. propose config: `perf.regression_gate = { "window": "5m", "p99_pct": 8, "absolute_ms": 150 }`. Will add defaults to canary rollout.

Eva: thanks, will sync with product on rollout risk. :thumbsup:

Ravi: I'll open two PRs: one for kernel_fallback metric + tracing hooks, one for the apples-vs-replay runbook and small-sample artifact. assigning to @Jules and @Samir for review.

Jules: ack, will pick up kernel metric PR today.

perf-bot: Note: tagging run results with label `kv-warmup-investigation`.

Ravi: closing notes: don't trust synth-only p99 unless KV warmup semantics and kernel-fallback counters are validated. plan to re-run after metrics PR lands and update the report.
